why_angle: The cited rival pages give inverter output only in VA or W. I opened Solar Waypoint, PluginSolarCheck, Solar United Neighbors and APsystems' pages, and none of them converts those ratings to amps on the house circuit. None checks the totals against the EZ1-LV's dedicated 10 A circuit condition or works out how much current breaker masking can let through. None points out that APsystems' own claim of '2 units on a standard 15A circuit' (15 A) is more than that condition allows. This page adds the current figures from the makers and retailers, the arithmetic, Hoymiles' plug and shutdown timings, and the CEC efficiencies.
must: its 900 VA puts 7.5 A on the wall outlet circuit

page.h1: Best plug-in solar inverter: how much current each one puts on your outlet circuit
page.desc: APsystems EZ1-LV vs Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV: amps at 120 V, the circuit each UL 3700 listing assumes, panel input limits, CEC efficiency and today's prices.
page.answer: Short answer. The best plug in solar inverter for two panels is the APsystems EZ1-LV microinverter: its 900 VA puts 7.5 A on the wall outlet circuit, inside the dedicated 10 A circuit its UL 3700 listing calls for. For one panel, a Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV adds 3.0–3.5 A.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Current on the circuit. Rated output ÷ 120 V: 900 VA ÷ 120 V = 7.5 A for the EZ1-LV; 420 VA ÷ 120 V = 3.5 A for the HMS-420; 360 VA ÷ 120 V = 3.0 A for the HMS-360.
  • Headroom on a dedicated 10 A circuit. One EZ1-LV: 7.5 A ÷ 10 A = 75%. Two EZ1-LVs: 2 × 7.5 A = 15 A, which is 1.5 times that 10 A condition and the full rating of a 15 A circuit.
  • Two panels, same retailer, same day. One EZ1-LV costs $281.78 for 900 VA. Two HMS-420s cost 2 × $157.51 = $315.02 for 840 VA. The EZ1-LV is $33.24 cheaper and gives 60 VA more. Per VA: $281.78 ÷ 900 = $0.31, against $157.51 ÷ 420 = $0.375.
  • Efficiency. California Energy Commission weighted efficiency: 95.5% − 95% = 0.5 point, about 5 kWh more per 1,000 kWh of panel output for the Hoymiles. That is too small to decide between them.
  • Panel fit. The EZ1-LV takes 18 A per input. The HMS-360, 391 and 420 take 14 A, so a panel rated above 14 A is current-limited on them. Hoymiles' 450 and 500 VA models take 15 A and 16 A.

How much current each inverter adds to your outlet circuit

A circuit breaker measures only the current coming from the panel. A plug-in inverter feeds its current in at the outlet, so appliances on the same circuit can draw from both sources at once. Solar United Neighbors puts it this way: added generation "can mask or hide the overloaded wiring so the breaker box does not trip the circuit off", and wiring can overheat as a result. Worst case on a 15 A circuit, with loads beyond the inverter's outlet: the wire between them can carry 15 A + 7.5 A = 22.5 A with one EZ1-LV, 15 A + 15 A = 30 A with two, or 15 A + 3.5 A = 18.5 A with one HMS-420. The breaker still sees no more than 15 A.

That is why the EZ1-LV's CSA certificate to UL 3700, as PluginSolarCheck quotes it, requires a latching PIPV plug and receptacle and a dedicated 10 A circuit, or a listed bidirectional Class A GFCI on a shared circuit. APsystems' consumer page says two EZ1 units can run "on a standard 15A circuit". At 2 × 7.5 A = 15 A, that is more than the 10 A dedicated-circuit condition. Buy one unit per circuit unless an electrician confirms otherwise.

Hoymiles says the HiFlow Pro mitigates breaker masking but does not explain how. Hoymiles also says the unit stops producing power within 135 ms of a grid outage. Solar United Neighbors gives 160 ms as the limit plug-in systems must meet.

Not recommended

EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter ($369.00 at EcoFlow's US store, 2026-11-10). EcoFlow's store copy lists UL 1741, not UL 3700, and says plug-in installation is currently permitted only in Utah, Maryland, Connecticut and Colorado. It has no 120 V row on California's grid-support inverter list, which includes the EZ1-LV and the HiFlow Pro LV 360/391/420.
